A massive laser-cutter carves a glowing trench across the rock face, throwing a fan of white-hot sparks that drift and die in the vacuum.
A battered ore-hauler hangs at a conveyor, its hold yawning open as crushed rock pours in under floodlights thick with dust.
A blast charge detonates deep in the rock in a silent flowering of debris, a shockwave of dust expanding slowly in the dark.
A rotary drill bores deep into the asteroid face, its tungsten bit grinding through ancient stone while fine grey powder billows in slow clouds.
A crane swings a loaded cargo container across the operation yard, the massive steel box spinning lazily on its cable in the zero-g.
A swarm of drones chews at an exposed seam, each unit biting off thumbnail-sized chunks that tumble into collection nets stretched below.
A stubby tug tows a house-sized chunk of separated rock toward the processing platform, thrusters burning orange against the absolute black behind it.
Two workers wrestle a heavy feed pipe into alignment, boots locked to the deck, their suits straining as the coupling finally seats with a shudder.
A bucket-wheel excavator grinds along the ore face, its spinning teeth tearing loose cascades of glittering rock that fall onto the belt below.
Molten slag pours from the smelter's tap-hole in a slow orange river, cooling instantly at its edges into black crust as it flows into the mold.
A robotic arm strips a freshly blasted wall, scooping rubble into a hopper in rhythmic sweeps while warning lights strobe red across the dust.
A pressurized ice-melt pump drives superheated water into a fissure, cracking the surrounding rock with a shiver that rolls through the entire face.
A magnetic separator pulls iron-bearing ore from the belt stream, the dark fragments snapping sideways in a sudden clean arc toward the collection drum.
A survey drone skims the asteroid surface, painting the terrain with ranging lasers, its sensor pod tilting and nodding like a curious bird.
A plasma torch cuts through a seized drill-collar, the brilliant cutting arc throwing shadows hard and sharp across the helmets of the watching crew.
A rock-bolting machine fires anchor rods into the tunnel ceiling, each shot punching through fractured stone to lock the structure against collapse.
A conveyor belt hauls crushed ore up a steep incline toward the transfer station, its rubber surface groaning under the shifting weight of the load.
A pressurized blasting crew retreats from a freshly drilled borehole, unreeling detonator wire hand over hand as the rock face recedes behind them.
A crawler-mounted crusher receives a dumped load of raw rock, its jaws cycling open and closed, reducing boulders to gravel in seconds.
A coring machine pulls a long cylindrical sample from the face, the crew rotating the slender tube under their helmet lamps, reading the layered rock.
A refinery module vents processed gas in a long pale plume, the exhaust catching the distant sunlight and scattering it in a brief ghostly rainbow.
A loader scoops a fresh pile of blasted rubble, its bucket biting deep, then pivots and dumps the load rattling down a chute into darkness.
A maintenance crew patches a cracked pipeline segment, wrapping it in composite tape under the blue flicker of a curing lamp in the tunnel shadow.
A winch hauls a broken drill-string up from a deep borehole, the long steel sections emerging one by one, slick with drilling fluid and grime.
An automated assay unit ingests a rock sample and spits its verdict on the crew's displays, numbers scrolling fast while the supervisor leans in close.
